solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Confirm wild animal has escaped

parts.note: a bear is a wild animal
an animal that has escaped is out

explanation.surface: A zoo confirms that one of its wild animals has got loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something out is to support or corroborate it, which is to confirm it.

clue.text: Girl bather in trouble and out of breath

indicators.note: someone in trouble is in a mess, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl swimming gets into difficulty and is gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of breath' is a second anagram of the same letters: BREATH rearranged gives the girl's name too.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Checks the accuracy of someone else's accounts

definitions.text: Checks the accuracy of someone else's accounts

parts.words: Checks the accuracy of someone else's accounts
parts.note: a description of the official inspection of a firm's financial books by an outsider

explanation.surface: An accountant verifies the books kept by another person.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor formally examines financial records to verify their accuracy.

clue.text: First former?

parts.note: looks like a pupil in the first form at a British school, but read literally is the first one to form something

explanation.surface: A question about a child in the lowest class of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'first former' is a British term for a pupil in the first year (form) of secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who first creates or forms something is its creator or inventor.

clue.text: Object of night out?

indicators.note: out suggests the letters have been put out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about the purpose of an evening on the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object or item.

clue.text: Big shot in the film world?

definitions.text: Big shot in the film world?

parts.words: Big shot in the film world?
parts.note: reads like a celebrity in the movies, but means a camera shot in which the subject looks big because it is filmed from very near

explanation.surface: A question about who counts as a VIP in the movie business.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shot taken at very short range makes its subject fill the screen, so it is literally a big shot.

clue.text: Victor — or William?

definitions.meaning: one who wins, a winner in battle
William I, the Norman duke who invaded England in 1066, is known by this title

explanation.surface: Asking whether the winner was the man called Victor or the one called William.
explanation.walkthrough: Both look like men's names; only William is one here, as William the Conqueror, who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is one who overcomes an enemy; William of Normandy took the epithet after conquering England.

clue.text: Finished in government

definitions.meaning: ruling or in authority above others, as in being set above a people

explanation.surface: A minister's career is finished while still in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished is over; to be over a people is to be in charge of governing them.

clue.text: Could be next Open champion, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A golfer who might win the next Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next Open' looks like the golf tournament; its letters are the fodder. 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate or champion of a cause is one who promotes it, an example of this meaning.

clue.text: Go into liquidation when working hard

definitions.text: Go into liquidation when working hard

parts.words: Go into liquidation when working hard
parts.note: sounds like a business going bust, but means turning to liquid, sweating, during heavy effort

explanation.surface: A firm collapses into insolvency while working flat out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat is to give off liquid through the skin, typically during hard exertion.

clue.text: They meet in the centre of the ring

definitions.text: They meet in the centre of the ring

parts.words: They meet in the centre of the ring
parts.note: sounds like boxers meeting mid-ring, but describes the lines from a circle's middle to its edge, which all meet at the centre

explanation.surface: Two boxers come together in the middle of the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines running from a circle's circumference to its middle all converge at the centre point.

clue.text: A host of local supporters

parts.note: reads as a crowd of home fans, but 'local' is the British word for a neighbourhood pub, and its host is the landlord

explanation.surface: A large crowd of home fans turns out for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A host of' looks like 'many'; here host is the person running the place. A 'local' is a Briton's regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord of a pub or inn hosts its regular drinkers, the people of the local.

clue.text: Losing a point at tennis but going for runs at cricket

definitions.meaning: a tennis player who sends the ball beyond the lines loses the point
a cricket batsman who swings boldly to score runs quickly is batting aggressively

explanation.surface: A sportsman drops a point on the tennis court but scores freely in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs are the points scored by batsmen; batting this way means attacking the bowling with big shots.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, striking the ball past the lines loses the point; in cricket the same phrase means batting aggressively.

clue.text: Cut the bird's tail off

indicators.note: taking the tail off means removing the last letter of the bird's name

parts.note: a snipe is a wading bird with a long bill; the 's is the link 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone trims the tail feathers off a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors, and to snip is to cut.

clue.text: They manipulate people to their advantage

definitions.text: They manipulate people to their advantage

parts.words: They manipulate people to their advantage
parts.note: sounds like exploiters, but describes practitioners who physically manipulate bones and joints for the patient's benefit

explanation.surface: Schemers use other people for their own gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' seems to point to the manipulators; it means the patients being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: These practitioners treat patients by manipulating the bones, joints and muscles to ease pain.

clue.text: Catch fighting?

parts.note: reads as if one might catch or stumble upon a brawl, but means capturing an enemy during a battle

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they might happen upon a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Capturing an enemy soldier during a war is to catch someone in the course of fighting.

clue.text: Height of architectural front?

definitions.meaning: an architect's drawing of one face of a building, often the front

explanation.surface: Asking how tall the facade of a building is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means altitude, and also an architect's flat drawing of a building's face.

clue.text: Radio executive sets up record

definitions.meaning: the person in broadcasting in charge of making a programme
in the music business, the person who oversees the making of a recording

explanation.surface: A broadcasting boss arranges a recording session.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person oversees and organises a broadcast programme or a music recording.

clue.text: Guess I'm in property

indicators.note: in places the letters of I'm inside the word for property

parts.note: an estate is land or property owned by someone
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone estimates their own place in the property market.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is a rough calculation or guess.

clue.text: Bring back discipline and revive fraternity

definitions.meaning: to bring back to life a religious brotherhood or society, an order

explanation.surface: A reformer wants to bring back strict rules and renew the brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate calm after unrest, or literally to re-establish a monastic brotherhood or society.

clue.text: Writer has way to tuck in inside French restaurant

indicators.note: tucking in inside means putting the street abbreviation within the pen

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, something you write with
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A writer finds a way into a French restaurant to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRO, a British name for a ballpoint pen, is a writer in crossword terms; 'tuck in' also suggests eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal French-style restaurant.

clue.text: Fire when an explosive's not set?

indicators.note: not removes the word for set from the explosive

parts.note: gelignite is a high explosive; the 's stands for 'is'
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Lighting an explosive when it hasn't been properly prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to set it on fire.

clue.text: Platform is said to be unstable

indicators.note: something unstable wobbles and shifts, so the letters of the word before move around

explanation.surface: A stage is reported to be wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform for speakers or dignitaries at one end of a hall.

clue.text: Sea water that's in one's watch

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
a spring is a source of water rising from the ground

explanation.surface: Seawater has somehow got inside someone's wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The coiled spring that drives a mechanical watch is the part found inside one.

clue.text: The more of them one has, the more one wants

definitions.text: The more of them one has, the more one wants

parts.words: The more of them one has, the more one wants
parts.note: sounds like a saying about greed, but literally having more requirements means wanting more things

explanation.surface: A proverb about desire growing with possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are things one wants, so having many of them means lacking many things.

clue.text: Two notes to measure

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
te (or ti) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician measures out a couple of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to measure or allot portions, as of punishment.

clue.text: Unusually fierce sea battle ends with it

indicators.note: something done unusually is done differently from the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exceptionally ferocious naval battle comes to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce or halt to the shooting is what brings a battle to its end.

clue.text: All the composer required

definitions.meaning: an Italian word for everyone, everything
a musical direction on a score telling all the players to perform together

explanation.surface: Everything the composer asked for was provided.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'all', used on scores as an instruction that the full orchestra plays together.

clue.text: Read one novel in girls' school

indicators.note: novel means new or different, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Pupils read a work of fiction at a girls' school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being read; it is the anagram signal. ROEDEAN is a famous English girls' boarding school near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known independent boarding school for girls on the Sussex coast of England.

clue.text: It contracts to continue one's circulation

definitions.text: It contracts to continue one's circulation

parts.words: It contracts to continue one's circulation
parts.note: sounds like a newspaper signing deals to keep its readership, but describes the heart's squeezing phase that pumps blood round the body

explanation.surface: A magazine signs deals so as to keep up its sales.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle squeezes, pushing blood around the body.
